subject: Service assurance banding & exception request — CloudArc migration
body:
From: Priya Desai <p.desai@cloudarc.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 27 Sep 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Request: SLA banding + monthly credit schedule for Sept migration

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We’re moving forward with the Sept→Oct migration and procurement is asking us to get a tailored SLA amendment in place before cutover. Two asks from our side:

1) Temporary adjustment to the uptime target during the migration window — our infra team would like clarity on acceptable availability during the two-week ramp (we expect some latency spikes during bulk KV warming). Specifically: can Redwood agree to a temporary floor of 99.9% for October (instead of your standard 99.95) with clear maintenance carveouts for scheduled migration tasks?

2) Monthly credit schedule — procurement needs a simplified, predictable credit band for the first three months post-cutover. They prefer:
  - 99.99–100%: no credit
  - 99.95–99.989%: 5% of monthly invoice
  - 99.9–99.949%: 20%
  - <99.9%: 50% credit (with a cap at one month’s invoice)

Our goal is speed: if we can agree to an amendment this week we’ll proceed with signing and schedule the migration. I’ve attached our migration plan and a redline of your standard SLA with our suggested changes.

Attachments: CloudArc_migration_plan.xlsx; Redwood_SLA_template_redline_v2.pdf

Best,
Priya Desai
Head of Cloud Operations, CloudArc

---

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Desai <p.desai@cloudarc.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 27 Sep 2026 13:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: SLA banding + monthly credit schedule for Sept migration

Hi Priya — thanks for the clear note and the migration plan. Appreciate the heads-up on the KV warming risk. We can move quickly on this, but need to align internally on deviations from our standard template. A few immediate items:

- Standard Redwood hosted availability is 99.95% with our published credit bands (we typically cap credits at 100% monthly invoice and include scheduled maintenance carveouts for announced windows).
- Two practical options I can propose quickly for your runbook:
  1) Temporary floor approach: Redwood signs a short-term amendment that accepts 99.9% for the month of October only, explicitly excluding agreed scheduled migration windows and with credits capped at 30% for that month.
  2) Credit-banding approach: Keep standard 99.95% uptime, but adopt your proposed credit bands for the first three months, with a cap of 50% of monthly invoice. This keeps the baseline SLO but gives predictability on credits.

I’m looping in Laura for approval on any one-off caps and vivo (Vivek) for final sign-off if we need to go beyond standard credit caps. Ben — can you confirm whether Finance is OK with a temporary 50% cap for three months if we take option 2?

I’ll draft an amendment once we pick an option — can you confirm which you prefer (temporary floor vs. banding) and whether CloudArc will accept a requirement for a single migration maintenance window per week to be excluded (timebox to 4 hours)?

Thanks —
Rachel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

---

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 27 Sep 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: SLA banding + monthly credit schedule for Sept migration

Team — quick decision: we should accept a constrained, time-limited exception to keep the deal moving but guard downside and precedent. My direction:

- Approve option 1 (temporary floor) but with these constraints:
  * Effective only for the single month of October 2026 (customer must sign amendment prior to cutover).
  * Uptime floor: 99.9% for October only.
  * Credits for October capped at 30% of that month’s invoice (no cumulative carryover).
  * One weekly migration maintenance window (up to 4 hours) agreed in writing; any additional unannounced maintenance will not be carved out.
  * CloudArc must enable our additional tracing hooks/agent during the migration window (we will provide a read-only collector) and accept extra monitoring telemetry for the duration.

- Require a formal amendment (SLA Addendum) and an exec sponsor sign-off (ops lead + procurement). No precedent-setting language beyond the explicit date range.

Vivek — ok to sign this off on behalf of Product/GT if legal gives the green light with that cap? Ben — confirm Finance acceptance of 30% cap for one month. If both green, Rachel send the amendment to CloudArc and DocuSign link.

Laura
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference

---

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Desai <p.desai@cloudarc.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: SLA banding + monthly credit schedule for Sept migration

Hi Priya — looping back with our approved approach. Per internal review we can approve a one-month, timeboxed amendment for October with the following terms:

- Uptime floor for October 2026: 99.9% (temporary amendment).
- Credit schedule for October: any availability below 99.9% will trigger credits up to a cap of 30% of that month’s invoice.
- One agreed weekly migration maintenance window (max 4 hours). Any additional maintenance must be announced 72 hours in advance to be carved out.
- CloudArc to enable Redwood tracing hooks/agent for the migration window and accept monitoring telemetry for the duration (our engineering team will share the collector and read-only access).
- Amendment is limited to Oct 1–31, 2026 and will not apply beyond that period. After October we revert to standard 99.95% SLO and published credit bands unless we mutually agree otherwise in writing.

I’ve attached a short SLA Addendum reflecting the above (Redwood_SLA_template_redline_v2.pdf). If this matches your needs, please execute via DocuSign here: https://www.docusign.com/link/abc123-docu_sign and confirm the agreed weekly maintenance window (suggest Wednesdays 02:00–06:00 UTC).

Next steps:
- Priya: confirm acceptance and preferred weekly maintenance slot by EOD 28 Sep so we can start the migration onboarding.
- Ben: I’ve asked Finance to clear the 30% cap for October — will update by EOD.

If you prefer the banding approach instead, we can discuss but it will take an extra 24–48 hours to get legal to adjust the cap.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0116
